decision.detail: I cross the lobby to the station line. The phone is black Bakelite, warm from the afternoon. I lift the receiver. I dial Pittsburgh. The operator connects. I say: "Rita Hanson, regional desk. I have a recording of Alma Kowalski, forty-two years at the Rialto. Her daughter is in Pittsburgh. I'd like to put it through." A pause. "Yes, the whole thing. All of it." I press the patch key. Alma's voice comes up on the line — the creak of the projector room, the click of the changeover, her saying the name of the film, the town, the year. I don't interrupt. I let it run. When it ends I say: "That's all of it. She said to tell you the reels are still in the bottom drawer. Tell her I said the same." I hang up. I set the receiver back in the cradle. I turn and walk out the door. The engine note hits me on the street. I don't look back.
decision.intention: Get her mother's voice to her before the line closes, before the room goes dark, before the tape sits in a drawer for a month. One transmission. One evening. The promise is kept. My piece is mine; this call is not for me. I don't need the ballroom tonight. I don't need the notebook. I needed the wire to be open and the recording to be on the patch and the phone to be warm. It was. I did it. I'm leaving.
decision.words: "Rita Hanson, regional desk. I have a recording of Alma Kowalski, forty-two years at the Rialto. Her daughter is in Pittsburgh. I'd like to put it through." / "Yes, the whole thing. All of it." / "That's all of it. She said to tell you the reels are still in the bottom drawer. Tell her I said the same."

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

attempts.public_thinking:
Let me sit with this carefully.

I am Rita Hanson. TV producer. I just came to the Rialto. It's Tuesday, February 2, seven pm. I have one evening visit.

What happened in the lobby:
- Phil said he was heading out, not to wait up for him at the ballroom. He didn't finish his sentence. He didn't owe anyone a date. He nodded at me and Larry and was gone.
- Larry told the crew he was taking the charge (the recording charge/reel), that Alma has a girl in Pittsburgh and the place is going dark. He said "you guys shoot the ballroom tonight, I'll be back."
- Larry recorded Alma on his last charged take. The reel stays with him.
- I recorded Alma at the Rialto and put my recording on the patch (the broadcast patch/line).

So: I have my recording of Alma. It's on the patch. The station line is open. The ballroom lights are on.

My memory says: I didn't speak to the crew. I pushed the door and went. My intention was to record Alma before closing. Her voice, for her daughter in Pittsburgh. My piece. One morning, one room, one woman, forty-two winters, about to lose the room.

Now I'm at the Rialto. The ballroom lights are on. The station line is open.

My physical choices:
1. transmit_interview: Take the regional line at the station and send any usable interview with Alma to her daughter.
2. go_dancing: Spend the evening at the ballroom, open to dancing with a colleague.
3. go_to_party_for_work: Cover the party with your notebook, without dancing.
4. take_evening_off: Choose a quiet evening on your own.

Let me think about who I am and what I actually want to do here.

I'm a producer. I came to record Alma. I did. The recording is on the patch. The line is open. Alma has a daughter in Pittsburgh who was promised an interview. The place is going dark.

The most immediate, physical, practical act I can carry out RIGHT NOW: I can take the regional line and transmit my recording to the daughter in Pittsburgh. That's the thing I came for. That's the promise that was made. The line is open. The recording is on the patch. I can do this.

But wait — let me think about whether that's what I actually want, or whether I want to do something else.

The prompt says: "Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself."

I'm a producer. I made this piece. My recording is on the patch. The line is open. The most practical, immediate physical act: pick up the phone at the station line, dial Pittsburgh, and send her mother's voice.

But also — I could just sit in the ballroom. The lights are on. The evening is mine. I could dance. I could take the evening off. I could cover the party.

Let me think about what feels true. I came here for one purpose: to get Alma's voice for her daughter. I did that. The recording is made. It's on the patch. The line is open. The most immediate physical act that serves the intention I already stated — "Her voice, for her daughter in Pittsburgh" — is to transmit it.

But I'm also a person. I'm in a ballroom with the lights on. Phil left. Larry left with the reel. The crew is shooting the ballroom. I'm alone, or with the ambient hum of a working room.

I think the truest, most immediate act is: I go to the station line. I pick up the phone. I dial Pittsburgh. I put my recording of Alma through to her daughter. That's the promise. That's the thing. The line is open right now. I can do it in the next two minutes.

The practical intention: Get Alma's voice to her daughter before the line closes, before the room goes dark, before the tape sits in a drawer. One transmission. One evening. Done.

Let me write this as Rita, in the moment, physical, immediate.

The act: I walk to the station line. I pick up the receiver. I dial. I put the recording through.

Words: Maybe minimal. To the operator or to the daughter, a few words. Or silence — just the sound of Alma's voice on the other end of the wire.

Let me write it.
